ImageDescription.value: Gorée is the island off the coast of Sénégal from where much of the Atlantic slave trade took place. The Door of No Return, through which people were taken to work in the Americas and other nearby colonies, is visible in the red brick building on the left, known as the House of Slaves and today serving as a museum.

title: File:2022-08-27 04 Silhouette sculpture of Norsemen above L'Anse aux Meadows, NFL CAN.jpg

ObjectName.value: 2022-08-27 04 Silhouette sculpture of Norsemen above L'Anse aux Meadows, NFL CAN

Categories.value: L'Anse aux Meadows|Self-published work|Information field template with formatting|Heritage properties in Canada with known IDs|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2024|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-ca|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC source of file|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2024 in Canada|Norsemen silhouette sculpture

ImageDescription.value:
Norse silhouette sculpture above L'Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site, Newfoundland Canada on August 27, 2022.

This sculpture commemorates the arrival of the Vikings in approximately 1021 and was designed by New Brunswick artist, Karen Van Niekerk. It is made of corten steel, 10 millimeters thick and approximately 2.4 meters high,

Most of the Norse figures look southeast to symbolize their intent to use L’Anse aux Meadows as a base camp to explore further southward from Newfoundland's Great Northern Peninsula. One looks back to southern Greenland from whence they came. There is a woman figure indicative of families that came during the period that L'Anse aux Meadows was used as a base camp.
